LESSON: LINEAR INEQUALITIES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Algebra 2.2 Equations of Straight Lines (15 lessons) • Gradient of a line • Equa
Topic 2.3: Linear Inequalities

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Linear Inequalities. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we represent linear inequalities in graphs?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. solve linear inequalities in one unknown

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Linear Inequalities.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Linear Inequalities using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss why sometimes resources are shared unequally.
2. Discuss simple inequality statements, form and work out the inequalities in one unknown.
3. Discuss and generate a table of values and draw linear inequalities in one unknown. Indicate and discuss the region that satisfies the inequalities.
4. Discuss and generate a table of values and draw linear inequalities in two unknowns. Indicate and discuss the region that satisfies the inequalities.
5. Discuss and work out linear inequalities that involve real-life cases

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we represent linear inequalities in graphs?
2. How do we use linear inequalities in real-life situations?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Linear Inequalities is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
